title: FiLM-to-Mirror hierarchy with fused Givens inference
hypothesis: Shared FiLM state plus small per-function Givens views will recover hierarchical context-specific affine functions with lower bytes than independent FiLM/full affine while fused-kernel throughput remains at least 0.80x independent FiLM.
mirror_coordinate: Eight disjoint pairwise Givens angles per logical function
logical_multiplicity: Eight context-specific affine functions from one shared FiLM state
controls: native shared FiLM + Givens angle adapter

world.operator_codes: oracle teacher codes; no task adaptation is claimed

development.selection_metric: max per-function NRMSE, actual serialized bytes, fused-kernel throughput ratio

training.state_construction: closed-form teacher codes, oracle diagonal least-squares projection, rank-4 SVD residual

paid_objects: NPZ arrays and metadata per method/world
shared FiLM state for tied methods
storage.free_state: Givens sin/cos derived from saved angles during model load; no cached table is serialized

compute.kernel: compiled C; fused FiLM + disjoint Givens

success_gate: Both development worlds: Mirror max per-function NRMSE <= 0.01, payload <= 0.75x independent FiLM and <= 0.10x full affine, and fused Mirror throughput >= 0.80x independent FiLM.
failure_gate: Any development quality/storage/runtime gate misses, or a native ordinary control exactly aliases Mirror code/output.
boundaries: Fresh worlds remain sealed after any dev gate miss
Native Givens adapter is a direct alias counter-control
No neural-language or natural task capacity claim
